summary.en-GB: Removes the sign-up, log-in and install-the-app popups that x.com puts in front of logged-out visitors, and makes the page scroll again.

description.en-GB:
Reading x.com without an account means fighting a wall of popups: "Continue to X", "Scan to get the app", surprise log-in dialogs and, on phones, "Get the full app experience". Hiding them with an element-hiding filter leaves the page frozen, because X also locks scrolling. This add-on dismisses them properly and keeps the page scrollable. What it removes
  • The "Continue to X" wall at the bottom of profiles and posts.
  • The "Scan to get the app" QR code popup.
  • Log-in and sign-up dialogs that open on their own, or when X takes over a click on a post, Like or Follow.
  • The "Don't miss what's happening" popup shown instead of the post you clicked. The post opens instead.
  • The "Log in or sign up for X" box in the sidebar, and the Google one-tap sign-in overlay.
  • On phones: the "Get the full app experience" / "Open X" popup, and tweet links that send you to the app store instead of the post.
  • Cookie banners, by choosing "Refuse non-essential cookies" where offered.
What it leaves alone If you click "Log in" or "Sign up" yourself, that dialog stays open, so you can still log in. For actions that need an account, such as Like, a small notice explains why nothing happened. Privacy It only runs on x.com and twitter.com, collects no data and sends nothing anywhere. It needs access to those sites to rewrite app-store redirect links back to normal x.com links. Works in Firefox on desktop and Android. The source code is on GitHub. This add-on is not made, endorsed or supported by X Corp.

release_notes.en-GB:
• Opens the post you clicked instead of X's "Don't miss what's happening" popup.
  • Hides the "Log in or sign up for X" box in the sidebar.
  • Shows a small notice when an action needs an account.
  • Fixes "Something went wrong" when opening profiles from posts.
  • Fixes the page not scrolling on mobile when a cookie banner is shown, and tweet links opening the app store.
